_about: TRANSLATOR SHELF: Lafcadio Hearn (1850-1904) as translator. Gautier's One of Cleopatra's Nights and Other Fantastic Romances (1882) Flaubert's The Temptation of St. Anthony (published 1910) and Anatole France's The Crime of Sylvestre Bonnard (1890). PD. His own Japanese books are not shelved. Added 2026-10-03 by lane C (round 8) under the coordinator's standing instruction; Adam may veto the whole shelf. No uids minted in the relay burst.

hearn-france-the-crime-of-sylvestre-bonn.scan_edition: Harper & Brothers, New York and London, "Copyright, 1890"; the title page prints no year and the library call number reads 1890. The text is Hearn's 1890 translation; he died in 1904, so no later printing can carry new matter by him

_excluded.pg-25053: Gutenberg 25053 is another Temptation of St. Antony with no translator named; not Hearn's.
_excluded.hearn-own-works: Kwaidan, Glimpses of Unfamiliar Japan etc.: Hearn's own books.
_excluded.pg-22660-22662: King Candaules, Clarimonde and The Mummy's Foot: single stories from One of Cleopatra's Nights (39397), already held whole.

_name_words_note: Translator name(s) only: fetch_shelf.py treats these as the identity check (one must appear in the fetched text), so the original author's name is deliberately NOT listed.
_verified_note: Evidence that each source's rights/identity line was read (lane C review fix, 2026-10-02, pipeline run over the fetched files; no book text recorded). PG: the header's Translator: line and the COPYRIGHTED marker. IA: whether the translator's name appears in the first 30 KB of OCR, and the years printed in the first 15 KB of front matter (scanner/digitizer lines skipped). Any post-1930 year there was examined by eye; see the title's scan_edition.
_surname_note: 2026-10-03: full printed names only, after Lane D's name audit (a bare one-word form would pass other authors of the same surname, e.g. Maude Ashurst Biggs). Tested against every source on the shelf; the only misses already carry _identity_checked overrides.
